assignment: Extract the exact GET /v1/fleet/roster JSON contract (fields, status vocabulary, capacity map shape) from api/lib/barkpark/tasks/fleet.ex + the Go structs, as the fleet card's data spec; and check whether cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/web/instance_api_proxy_test.exs already anticipates non-webhook capabilities.
verdict: GREEN on the contract extraction, ORANGE on the catalog question. Roster row shape is exactly 7 keys: worker, agent, scope, status, capacity, last_seen, ttl_s (plus a read-time-joined 'task' key = the worker's current in_progress doc_id or null) -- pinned by fleet_test.exs:112 (`field_names == ~w(worker agent scope status capacity last_seen ttl_s)`) and fleet.ex:183-197 (`to_row/3`). Status vocabulary is 5 values, NOT 'online': self-declared {idle, working, blocked} (fleet.ex:67), provisioner-written {provisioning} (fleet.ex:68, PDF-D23 -- a beat can never self-declare it), and read-time-derived {offline} (never stored). There is no literal 'online' string anywhere in the contract -- the wish's 'ONLINE flips on first heartbeat' means 'status reads anything-but-offline', not a stored enum member. Capacity is a discriminated union at the JSON level (fleet.ex:293-321): (a) a validated object {size_class: light|standard|heavy|xl, slots_total?, slots_free?, budget?} -- REFUSED at write time on any vocab/bounds violation (no silent-drop), (b) a JSON-object STRING that decodes+validates into the same shape (the CLI's --capacity path, since Go ships it as a query string), or (c) any other plain string, stored verbatim as a legacy free-form hint. A GUI fleet card must render capacity as 'object OR string', not assume one shape. On the Go side there is NO typed Roster/RosterRow struct anywhere in the repo (grep across internal/ found only cloud_support_cmd.go, which consumes the envelope as bare `map[string]any` (line 1509-1510) and does a manual `d["worker"].(string)` match) -- this is deliberate per PDF-D21 ('the documents envelope key every installed bp binary renders as a real table'), i.e. the roster is designed to be read generically, not through a typed client model; a new fleet-card SPA slice should follow the same untyped-JSON posture rather than inventing a Go struct that doesn't exist to mirror. On the catalog question: instance_api_proxy_test.exs (679 lines) is 100% webhook-scoped -- every describe block, every assertion, is webhook.* -- and grep for resource/capability/task/fleet inside it and inside instance_api_catalog_test.exs (214 lines) returns zero non-webhook hits. Worse than 'not anticipated': the PROXY ROUTER ITSELF hardcodes the envelope, not just the tests -- `json(conn, status, %{ok: true, resource: "webhook", data: ...})` at router.ex:8834 is a LITERAL STRING, not derived from `entry.capability` (the InstanceApiCatalog entry struct has no `resource` field at all -- only capability/method/path/tier/params). Two more hardcodings ride the same seam: the 404-degrades-to-capability_unavailable guard (router.ex:8845-8850) pattern-matches an explicit list of 4 webhook.* atoms with no fallback, and `instance_mutation_action/1` (router.ex:8948-8957) is a closed set of 6 webhook.* clauses with NO catch-all -- a new :mutate-tier capability (e.g. a hypothetical task.claim) would raise FunctionClauseError on its first successful write unless a clause is added. fleet.roster is :read-tier so it skips the audit-action function entirely, but still needs `resource: "webhook"` fixed or every fleet-card response will lie about its own resource type. CONCLUSION: existing test infra requires generalizing BOTH the envelope's resource string and (if any :mutate task capability ships) the audit-action total function before fleet.roster/task.get can slot in as new catalog rows -- this is source-level work, not test-only.
